```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Joshi_2017_vancomycin_rat"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Joshi_2017_vancomycin_rat"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12484> (open access, PMC5698807)
* Predecessor model from the same group, used to settle the units:
  <https://doi.org/10.1128/AAC.00591-16> (Rhodes 2016, PMC5038238)

The paper is primarily a bioanalytical method report (an HPLC-UV assay for
vancomycin in rat plasma and kidney homogenate, plus a catheter-adsorption
study). Its demonstration pharmacokinetic study fits a population model whose
final estimates are printed in Table 3; that model is what is packaged here.

# Population

Ten male Sprague-Dawley rats weighing 250-350 g were selected from a larger
nephrotoxicity study (Rhodes 2016) to illustrate the assay. Each received
vancomycin 150 mg/kg/day as a single daily intraperitoneal injection, for one
day (n = 5) or three days (n = 5). Plasma was sampled from a jugular-vein
catheter at 0 (predose), 10, 30, 60, 120, 240 and 1,440 min after the final
dose and assayed by HPLC-UV (lower limit of quantitation 3 mg/L, linear to
75 mg/L). The model was fitted with the non-parametric adaptive grid (NPAG)
algorithm in Pmetrics.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Joshi_2017_vancomycin_rat")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Structure: peritoneal depot, first-order absorption, fraction absorbed, two-compartment disposition with micro-constants | -- | Methods, 'Pharmacokinetic model'; Table 3 parameter list; Figure 4 title ('2 Compartment: Peritoneal, Rat, Vancomycin Model') |
| `lkel` (Ke) | log(0.911843) 1/h | Table 3, Ke mean |
| `lvc` (V) | log(0.185885) L | Table 3, V mean |
| `lka` (Ka) | log(3.946906) 1/h | Table 3, Ka mean |
| `lk12` (KCP) | log(45.33389) 1/h | Table 3, KCP mean |
| `lk21` (KPC) | log(42.25276) 1/h | Table 3, KPC mean |
| `logitfdepot` (FA1) | logit(0.459455) | Table 3, FA1 mean |
| `etalkel` | 0.555096 | Table 3, Ke SD 0.785514: log((SD/mean)^2 + 1) |
| `etalvc` | 0.501010 | Table 3, V SD 0.14991 |
| `etalka` | 0.230578 | Table 3, Ka SD 2.009931 |
| `etalk12` | 0.299421 | Table 3, KCP SD 26.78453 |
| `etalk21` | 0.450851 | Table 3, KPC SD 31.89025 |
| `etalogitfdepot` | 0.397883 | Table 3, FA1 SD 0.156658: (SD / (F (1 - F)))^2 (delta method) |
| `propSd`, `addSd` | fixed(0) | not reported |
| Units: time h, V in L for a 250-350 g rat, dose in mg | -- | not printed in Table 3; see 'Units' below |

# Units

Table 3 prints no units. Time is in hours: the Results report a median
half-life of 1.7 h, and the terminal half-life implied by the tabulated rate
constants is about 1.6 h (checked below). The volume could be either litres for
the whole rat (dosed with the absolute amount, 150 mg/kg times body weight) or
litres per kilogram (dosed in mg/kg). Two pieces of evidence select the first:

1. The ten rats are a subset of the Rhodes 2016 study, whose model of the
   same animals (Table 2) reports volume as 'liter/0.3 kg', i.e. litres for a
   0.3 kg rat dosed in mg. Rhodes 2016 did not estimate bioavailability; its
   median apparent values V/F = 0.3 L and CL/F = 0.3 x 0.9 = 0.27 L/h become
   about 0.14 L and 0.12 L/h after scaling by Joshi's fraction absorbed (0.46).
   Read as litres per rat, Joshi's Table 3 gives V = 0.19 L and
   CL = Ke x V = 0.17 L/h, the same order. Read as L/kg, the per-rat values
   would be 0.056 L and 0.051 L/h, 2.5-fold below the earlier fit.
2. The Discussion gives the mean predicted 6-h concentration in the one-day
   rats as 5.19 mg/L. The typical-value solve gives about 4.3 mg/L under the
   litre reading and about 14 mg/L under the L/kg reading.

The simulated cohort does not settle the question on its own: under the litre
reading its median Cmax and AUC fall about 55% below the Results' medians, and
under the L/kg reading they would sit about 45% above (see 'Comparison against
published NCA').

The model therefore takes the dose as an absolute amount in mg. The paper has
no body-weight covariate, so weight enters only through the dose.

# Typical-value checks

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Joshi_2017_vancomycin_rat")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

wt_ref <- 0.3 # kg, the middle of the 250-350 g range
dose_ref <- 150 * wt_ref # mg

ev_typ <- rbind(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose_ref, cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.01), seq(2, 48, by = 0.05)))),
    evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central"
  )
)
sim_typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame"))

# An independent implementation of the same system, written directly from the
# Table 3 parameterisation, to confirm the packaged model solves the
# intended structure (rxode2 may solve it in closed form from cl/vc/q/vp/ka).
indep <- rxode2::rxode2({
  d / dt(depot) <- -ka * depot
  d / dt(central) <- ka * depot - (ke + kcp) * central + kpc * peripheral1
  d / dt(peripheral1) <- kcp * central - kpc * peripheral1
  f(depot) <- fa
  Cc <- central / v
})
p_tab <- c(
  ke = 0.911843, v = 0.185885, ka = 3.946906,
  kcp = 45.33389, kpc = 42.25276, fa = 0.459455
)
sim_ind <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  indep,
  params = p_tab,
  events = rxode2::et(amt = dose_ref, cmt = "depot") |>
    rxode2::et(unique(ev_typ$time[ev_typ$evid == 0])),
  returnType = "data.frame"
))
chk <- dplyr::inner_join(
  sim_typ[, c("time", "Cc")],
  sim_ind[, c("time", "Cc")],
  by = "time", suffix = c("_pkg", "_ind")
)
rel_diff <- with(
  dplyr::filter(chk, Cc_ind > 0.01),
  max(abs(Cc_pkg - Cc_ind) / Cc_ind)
)

# Mass balance: cl * AUC(0-inf) must equal F * Dose (PKNCA AUC, not a
# hand-written trapezoid). With a terminal half-life near 1.6 h the profile
# has fallen by ~30 half-lives at 48 h, so AUC(0-48) is AUC(0-inf).
auc_inf <- PKNCA::pk.calc.auc.last(conc = sim_typ$Cc, time = sim_typ$time)
cl_typ <- 0.911843 * 0.185885
f_typ <- 0.459455

# Terminal half-life from the rate constants (beta phase of the disposition).
k10 <- 0.911843
k12 <- 45.33389
k21 <- 42.25276
beta <- ((k10 + k12 + k21) - sqrt((k10 + k12 + k21)^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
thalf_typ <- log(2) / beta

data.frame(
  check = c(
    "max relative difference, packaged vs independent ODE",
    "cl * AUC(0-inf) / (F * Dose)",
    "terminal half-life from Table 3 rate constants (h)",
    "typical Cmax (mg/L)",
    "typical C at 6 h (mg/L)"
  ),
  value = signif(c(
    rel_diff,
    cl_typ * auc_inf / (f_typ * dose_ref),
    thalf_typ,
    max(sim_typ$Cc),
    sim_typ$Cc[which.min(abs(sim_typ$time - 6))]
  ), 4)
) |>
  knitr::kable()

c6_typ <- sim_typ$Cc[which.min(abs(sim_typ$time - 6))]
stopifnot(
  # Same parameters on both sides: a pure numerical comparison.
  rel_diff < 1e-3,
  abs(cl_typ * auc_inf / (f_typ * dose_ref) - 1) < 0.01,
  # The Results' median half-life is 1.7 h.
  abs(thalf_typ / 1.7 - 1) < 0.15,
  # Discussion: mean predicted 6-h concentration 5.19 mg/L in the one-day
  # rats. The litre reading gives ~4.3 mg/L; the L/kg reading ~14 mg/L.
  abs(log(c6_typ / 5.19)) < log(1.5)
)
```

# Virtual cohort and simulation

Two arms of 100 rats each mirror the study: one daily dose (sampled over the
24 h after it) and three daily doses (sampled over the 24 h after the third).
Body weights are drawn uniformly over 250-350 g and each rat receives
150 mg/kg as an intraperitoneal injection into the depot.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20171101)
n_per_arm <- 100L

cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(2L * n_per_arm),
  arm = rep(c("1 day", "3 days"), each = n_per_arm),
  wt = stats::runif(2L * n_per_arm, 0.25, 0.35)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(n_dose = ifelse(arm == "1 day", 1L, 3L))

dose_rows <- cohort |>
  tidyr::uncount(n_dose, .id = "dose_no") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    time = (dose_no - 1) * 24, evid = 1L, amt = 150 * wt, cmt = "depot"
  )

obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.02), seq(2, 24, by = 0.1))))
obs_rows <- cohort |>
  dplyr::mutate(last_dose = (n_dose - 1) * 24) |>
  tidyr::crossing(tad = obs_grid) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = last_dose + tad, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dose_rows[, c("id", "time", "evid", "amt", "cmt")],
  obs_rows[, c("id", "time", "evid", "amt", "cmt")]
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(cohort[, c("id", "arm", "n_dose", "wt")], by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - (n_dose - 1) * 24)
```

# Replicate Figure 3

Figure 3 of the paper shows the observed mean (SEM) plasma concentrations for
all rats on a log axis: the one-day rats over 0-24 h and the three-day rats over
48-72 h. The simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles are plotted on the same
layout.

```{r figure3, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = stats::median(Cc),
    lo = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    hi = stats::quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  # Floor at the bottom of the plotted axis so the log scale has no zeros.
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(median, lo, hi), ~ pmax(.x, 1))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, median, group = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1, 300)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 72, by = 6)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (hours)", y = "Vancomycin concentration (mg/L)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 3 of Joshi 2017. Median and 5th-95th percentiles of",
      "100 simulated rats per arm; dashed line is the 3 mg/L LLOQ."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The observed means in Figure 3 peak near 100 mg/L after the single dose and
near 60 mg/L after the third dose, and fall to about 15 mg/L by 4 h. The
simulation reaches lower peaks (see the next section); the reasons are listed
under Assumptions and deviations.

# PKNCA validation

NCA is run on each rat's final dosing interval (0-24 h after the last dose),
grouped by arm.

```{r pknca}
# The stiff fast-distribution system can return values a few ulp below zero
# once the profile has decayed; those are set to zero rather than dropped.
conc_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, arm, tad, Cc)

dose_nca <- cohort |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, arm, tad = 0, dose = 150 * wt)

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, Cc ~ tad | arm + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, dose ~ tad | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 24,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
```

# Comparison against published NCA

The Results report, from the Bayesian posterior predicted concentrations over
24 h, a median Cmax of 69.9 mg/L (range 30.4-95.2), AUC of 254.6 mg*h/L
(range 194.2-307.0) and half-life of 1.7 h (range 1.5-5.9), pooled over both
arms. The Discussion separately gives a 24-h AUC of 264 mg*h/L for the one-day
rats.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- data.frame(
  arm = c("1 day", "3 days"),
  cmax = c(69.9, 69.9),
  auclast = c(254.6, 254.6),
  half.life = c(1.7, 1.7)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated (median of 100 rats per arm) vs the paper's pooled median",
    "Bayesian posterior NCA. * marks rows differing by >20%."
  )
)

sim_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::pull(PPORRES)
ratio_auc <- stats::median(sim_auc) / 254.6
ratio_auc

stopifnot(
  # Pins the documented shortfall rather than hiding it: the litre-per-rat
  # reading lands near 0.45, the L/kg reading (a dose 3.3x larger relative
  # to V) near 1.5, and a mis-transcribed V or Ke moves the whole
  # distribution out of this window. The median of 200 rats is robust to
  # RNG differences between rxode2 builds.
  ratio_auc > 0.3,
  ratio_auc < 0.8
)
```

The simulated half-life is within 9-26% of the paper's 1.7 h. Simulated Cmax and AUC
are roughly half of the paper's medians, and these rows are flagged. The
parameters were not adjusted to close the gap. The paper's values summarise the
individual Bayesian posterior profiles of ten rats, while the simulation draws
from independent log-normal marginals centred on the Table 3 means; with
coefficients of variation of 80-86% on Ke and V, the marginals are strongly
skewed and the medians of the fitted distributions are likely well below the
tabulated means. A Ke and a V each about 30% below their means would close the
AUC gap. The typical 6-h concentration (4.3 mg/L) is close to the 5.19 mg/L
the Discussion reports for the one-day rats.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Units were not printed.** Table 3 gives no units. Time in hours, volume in
  litres for a 250-350 g rat and the dose as an absolute amount in mg were
  inferred as described under 'Units'.
* **Non-parametric means carried as log-normal medians.** NPAG returns a
  discrete joint distribution of support points; Table 3 reports only the mean
  and SD of each marginal. Following the library's other Pmetrics models, each
  mean is the median of a log-normal (logit-normal for FA1) marginal, with the
  variance taken from SD/mean. The SDs are large (CV 51-86%), so the marginals
  are strongly skewed and the tabulated means are not the parameters of a
  typical rat. This is the most likely reason the simulated Cmax and AUC fall
  about 55% below the posterior medians reported in the Results.
* **Correlations are lost.** The joint NPAG distribution is not published, so
  the six random effects are independent. Ke and V, and KCP and KPC, are
  almost certainly correlated in the fitted support points.
* **Fraction absorbed on the logit scale.** FA1 (mean 0.459, SD 0.157) is
  carried as a logit-normal so that simulated fractions stay inside (0, 1); its
  variance was obtained from the SD by the delta method.
* **Residual error not reported.** The Pmetrics error model (gamma or lambda)
  and assay-error polynomial are not given; `propSd` and `addSd` are fixed to 0.
  The quoted fit statistics (R^2 0.98, bias -0.25 mg/L, imprecision
  1.05 mg^2/L^2) describe the individual Bayesian predictions in Figure 4.
* **Body weight.** The paper reports only the 250-350 g range; weights were
  drawn uniformly over it. There is no weight covariate in the model.
* **Figures 1, 2 and 4** (chromatograms, catheter-retention concentrations and
  the observed-vs-individual-predicted plot) cannot be reproduced from the
  model and are not replicated.
